Appearance:
 Shri Manish Yadav, Advocate for the applicant.
Shri Ritesh Kumar Sharma, Panel Lawyer for the non-ap  Shri Najesh Chouhan, Advocate for the objector.
ORDER Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is third application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C./483 of BNSS for grant of bail to the applicant in connection with FIR/Crime No.424/2023 dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station Azad Nagar, District Indore (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable u/S 363, 366-A and 376(2)(n) of IPC alongwith 3, 4 and 5(l)/6 of the POCSO Act.

sentences.text: 2. His first bail application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 09.02.2024 passed in MCRC No.3225/2024.
Thereafter, his second bail application was dismissed on merit vide order dated 22.05.2024 passed in MCRC No.20157/2024.
3. Prosecution story, in brief is that at the time of incident, prosecutrix was minor, aged around 16 years 04 months.

On 11.08.2023, applicant NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6501 2 MCRC-9036-2025 forcibly took the prosecutrix to Palda by motorcycle thereafter to many places and kept her alongwith him till 09.10.2023.
Meanwhile, he committed rape upon her repeatedly.
The prosecutrix was recovered on 10.09.2023.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant/accused submits that the applicant has not committed the offence and has falsely been implicated in the case.
It is submitted that prosecutrix lived with the applicant for around one month but she had never raised any alarm to rescue herself.
She was also a consenting party for sexual intercourse.
Applicant is in custody since 11.09.2023.
It is submitted that only 07 prosecution witnesses out of 12 witnesses have been examined before the Trial Court.
Both the parties have settled their dispute and at present, there is no dispute between them.
After completion of investigation, charge-sheet has been filed.
Trial will take considerable long time for its disposal, therefore, in the changed circumstances, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the non-applicant/State has opposed the prayer by submitting that second bail application of the applicant was dismissed on merit after considering the statement of prosecutrix (PW-1) and her father (PW-2).
The offence is serious in nature and also the offence is non-compoundable therefore, there is no change in the circumstances hence, the application is liable to be rejected.
6. Counsel for the objector has pleaded no objection in granting bail to the applicant.

7. Having considered the rival submissions and after perusal of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:6501 3 MCRC-9036-2025 case diary so also looking to overall facts and circumstances of the case, though, copy of compromise application has been filed by the applicant but the offence is non-compoundable and looking to the age of the prosecutrix, this Court is of the considered view that it is not a fit case to grant bail to the applicant.
Resultantly, this repeat bail application stands dismissed.

(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE gp Lakhan Sisodiya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52900831/
